capabilities: Show Git status grouped into staged, changed, untracked, deleted, renamed, and conflicted files in a sidebar
Open changed vault files directly in Obsidian
Commit explicitly selected files with a required message via a temporary Git index
Show the latest 50 commits with read-only commit details and changed files
Refresh status manually and after vault file events
extras: Deliberately scoped non-goals: no pull, push, clone, fetch, merge, rebase, branch management, stage/unstage, discard/reset, or conflict resolution. Makes no network requests; commit is its only write action. Installable from the community directory, manually, or via BRAT.
intentEvidence: without launching a heavier Git client or Visual Studio Code
motivation: Built for people who want to stay inside Obsidian, see which vault files changed, open those files, and commit intentionally without launching a heavier Git client.
problem: Obsidian users who want to see exactly which vault files changed and make intentional commits must otherwise open a heavier Git client or an editor like VS Code.

relations.evidence: without launching a heavier Git client or Visual Studio Code
For beta testing, install the plugin with BRAT using this repository URL

summary: Lightweight Git status and history viewer that commits only explicitly selected vault files through a temporary Git index.
